newsitem.title: INDIA: Reliance expands to bankroll doubled equity.
newsitem.headline: Reliance expands to bankroll doubled equity.

text.p: Strong earnings growth driven by huge increases in capacity would enable petrochemicals major Reliance Industries Ltd to bankroll a liberal bonus equity issue announced last week, analysts said.
They forecast net profit to rise between 20 percent and 50 percent during fiscal 1997/98 (April-March), helped by tripled capacity.

Jardine Fleming India Broking estimates 1997/98 net profit at 16.1 billion rupees ($550 million), up 22 percent from 13.2 billion in the year-earlier period, while HSBC Batlivala & Karani projects profits to rise 31 percent to 17.4 billion.
Bombay-based brokerage SSKI Securities put profit at 19.5 billion rupees, up 47.7 percent.
"The outlook is very good," said the executive director of a U.S.-based fund. "The bonus ratio took us by surprise, but it showed the company's extreme confidence in its future."
Reliance announced a one-for-one bonus issue -- a bonanza to its 2.6 million shareholders. The move also doubles its current share capital of 4.58 billion rupees.
The recommended bonus issue still has to be approved by an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders.

International investors hold 21 percent of Reliance equity, Indian financial institutions 19 percent, corporate bodies 28 percent, banks and mutual funds two percent and the balance of 30 percent is in individual investors' hands, according to Reliance figures.
Reliance is already one of the most liquid shares on Indian exchanges and the bonus issue will further increase liquidity, analysts said.
Reliance makes textiles and all basic petrochemical raw materials that go into them.

"We are the fifth-largest producer of polyester staple fibre in the world, the sixth-largest producer of polyester filament yarn and the 10th-largest producer of HPDE/LLDPE (high density polyethylene/linear low density polyethylene), chairman Dhirubhai Ambani told shareholders last week.

"With the completion of current projects at Hazira and Jamnagar (in the western state of Gujarat), we will emerge as the second-largest producer of paraxylene in the world, fifth-largest producer of polypropylene, third-largest producer of PTA (purified terephthalic acid) and the 10th-largest producer of MEG (mono ethylene glycol)," he said.
A 350,000 tonnes-per-year PTA plant and 120,000 tonnes MEG plant are scheduled to come on stream by end 1997, the company said.
Analysts said Reliance would have already tied up the 50 billion rupees in funding for its 1.4 million tonnes-a-year paraxylene project and 400,000 tonnes polypropylene plant.
On completion, by 1999 Reliance's total capacity would rise 50 percent to 9.3 million tonnes, the company said.
"I don't see major borrowings this year," said Sanjeev Prasad, analyst at Kotak Securities, the Indian associate of Goldman Sachs.

Ambani has promised to focus on enhancing shareholders' value by not diluting equity capital for another three years. He favoured a buy-back of stocks once a new law makes it possible and he set a target of 20 percent compound annual growth.
The Reliance stock, which has risen 80 percent this year compared to a 34 percent rise in the benchmark Bombay stocks index, is unlikely to make more progress, analysts said.
"For a commodity stock to quote above the market looks overvalued," said Kotak's Prasad. "We see it as a market performer."
